overall_assessment: The exact unapplied v2 proposal converges with no material findings. Independent inspection of the embedded original source and complete diff shows that the enforcement body and remaining methods are preserved verbatim under autenticar: public-route handling, cookie verification, current-user and password-change checks, mandatory password change before onboarding, session-before-CSRF ordering, usuario assignment and next remain unchanged. Noncallback requests delegate outside the callback catch, retaining their existing exceptions and statuses. For the packaged effective GET callback, the anchored case-insensitive req.path matcher admits only the named route and one optional trailing slash; it neither reads query data nor creates a public exemption. Callback confidentiality headers precede enforcement. Known denials map only to the three literal allowed classifications, while unexpected session or database exceptions before headers are sent map to the distinct INSTAGRAM_AUTHORIZATION_UNAVAILABLE classification. The fixed relative 303 destination and its fixed classifications expose no original URL, code, state, provider input, cookie or raw exception. Guard failures terminate before usuario assignment, next, controller or provider work. The headersSent branch preserves the genuine exception instead of attempting a second response. Successful admission retains the existing downstream session/state/CAS/grant obligations. The callback-specific normative 303 contract supports this specialization of the general BFF error statuses; ordinary routes retain their original contract. IG-OAUTH-SESSCOMP-01 is addressed at proposal level, including truthful distinction between infrastructure failure and authentication denial and the required fixed-text Numeros handling with the attempt kept pending. Performance is acceptable because the proposal adds only bounded local work and no I/O; elegance and structural soundness are acceptable because one callback boundary reuses the unchanged guard body without another authentication framework. Operational fit is acceptable for this proposal, with consumer and execution gates explicitly retained. Embedded-only reconstruction matches the declared original CRLF, exact-diff and candidate CRLF hashes; actual product-source identity, successful application and runtime behavior have not been verified. This is neither source/path admission nor implementation, delivery or runtime acceptance, and it does not close the complete IG-CP2-R1-04 or CP4 obligations.
recommended_path: Advance only this exact v2 proposal to the required explicit user validation of api-app/src/surfaces/bff/session.middleware.ts. This review grants no source-write or runtime authority. After that validation and the serialized handoff, the sole writer must recheck the actual source SHA-256 and CRLF bytes, apply the exact reviewed patch, verify the exact candidate hash and unchanged enforcement body, and retain required full-API and fresh-adherence gates. Prove actual Nest/PostgreSQL no-session, invalid-session, current-user/password and onboarding denials, password-before-onboarding precedence, successful session/state/CAS/grant enforcement, effective GET route case/trailing-slash parity and unchanged neighboring/noncallback status and CSRF behavior. Prove clean generic 303 outcomes at both real database lookup failure boundaries and unchanged equivalent noncallback error behavior, with confidentiality headers, safe Location/body and zero denied-path downstream facts/provider calls. Preserve real authentication, grants and transaction results; if an unexpected session-service failure cannot be induced by valid HTTP input, record the exact reached origin and limitation, with focused boundary fault evidence only as a supplement to actual session/PostgreSQL cases. Keep controller invalid-state, provider-error, expiry and other postmiddleware failures in their separate mandatory proof. Verify Numeros fixed handling of every allowed code and the infrastructure classification without false success, false authentication denial or attempt consumption. Complete the mandatory real-backend browser and gateway/query-log confidentiality proofs separately; embedded consistency and controller tests cannot substitute for them.
